categoryDetails.EIES: An environmental and social impact assessment identifies, assesses and ranks a project’s effects on the physical, biological and human environment, then defines the measures to avoid, reduce or offset them, set out in an environmental and social management plan submitted to the ACE.
categoryDetails.AUDIT: An environmental audit compares a site’s practices and facilities with regulatory requirements and the operator’s commitments, records any gaps and proposes a prioritised corrective action plan.
categoryDetails.MONITORING: Environmental monitoring tracks a site’s key parameters over time (water, air, soil, noise…) and consolidates the results in periodic reports for the operator and the authorities.
categoryDetails.AGREMENT: Support with approvals and certificates covers preparing and following up the regulatory files required to carry out an activity, until the document is issued by the competent authority.
categoryDetails.FORMATION: EWES training builds the skills of technical teams and institutions in environmental and social management, through sessions combining the regulatory framework, methods and practical cases.
categoryDetails.ETUDE: Studies and research produce data and analysis to support decision-making: field surveys, sector assessments and publications on environmental and social issues.

HomeAbout.title: Born at the university, proven in the field.
HomeAbout.lead: EWES grew out of the Environment Centre of the University of Lubumbashi–Society Interface, working with Belgian, French and Canadian partners. Its team brings together Congolese and international experts.
HomeAbout.text: The company has established itself in drawing up and assessing the environmental plans of mining and oil projects. It studies natural and man-made risks, develops sites, supports environmental compliance and trains the sector’s managers and technicians.
HomeAbout.imageAlt: EWES engineering team on a field mission

ServicesOverview.title: Three areas, one scientific standard.
ServicesOverview.aside: Each area builds on the previous one: environmental data shape water management, which in turn guides our engineering works.

Method.title: From sampling to report.
Method.text: We measure before we conclude: our recommendations rest on data collected, analysed and modelled locally.

steps.title: Regulatory scoping
steps.text: Analysis of the project and the applicable environmental obligations, then definition of the study scope.

steps.title: Fieldwork & sampling
steps.text: On-site surveys and sampling of water, soil and air.

steps.title: Laboratory & modelling
steps.text: Analyses, data processing and modelling of how the environment may evolve under different scenarios.

steps.title: Report, compliance & transfer
steps.text: Impact assessments, management plans, annual reports and remediation plans, followed by training for your teams so the results last.
